answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 26 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the haven solution is checked at the velvet gate and logged, the inlet audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch hence pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. A farm of 181 pays that 113 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
